source: FAO/OIE/World Bank, "Good Practices for Biosecurity in the Pig Sector - Issues and Options in Developing and Transition Countries", FAO Animal Production and Health Paper No. 169, Rome, 2010.
text: For farmers or extension workers with access to disinfectants, common options and their general properties: alcohol kills bacteria, most viruses and fungi but is flammable and has a strong odor; chlorine/bromine/iodine (halogen) disinfectants are effective against a broad range of pathogens including spores, but are irritating and reactive with other chemicals; quaternary ammonium compounds are effective against bacteria and enveloped viruses but less effective against spores; and acids are effective but corrosive. All disinfectants only work well after thorough physical cleaning has removed visible dirt and organic matter first.
caveat: This is a general property summary from an FAO/OIE/World Bank technical reference, not a product-specific usage guide - a farmer or extension worker should confirm correct dilution, contact time and safety precautions from the actual product label before use.
